question: What is the main goal of triage in a busy healthcare setting?

options.A: To sort patients and prioritize care based on urgency
options.B: To provide a complete medical diagnosis for every visitor
options.C: To collect insurance and billing information before treatment
options.D: To discharge minor cases without letting them see a doctor

explanation: Triage acts as your first safety filter when the ward is busy, ensuring the sickest patients get seen without dangerous delays. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to triage patients when the emergency department is packed?

options.A: Because hospital rules forbid seeing patients in the order they arrive
options.B: Because nurses need extra time to complete paperwork for each case
options.C: Because patient needs are greater than available staff and resources
options.D: Because doctors prefer to treat minor injuries before major trauma

explanation: When too many people arrive at once, triage helps match our limited hospital resources to the patients who need help the absolute most. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the golden rule of triage when responding to a major disaster?

options.A: Treating every single injured person in the exact order of arrival
options.B: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people
options.C: Sending all critical patients to the nearest small clinic
options.D: Focusing entirely on saving the person with the highest social status

explanation: In a disaster with scarce supplies, we shift our mindset from individual care to saving as many lives as our resources can possibly reach. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why must a triage nurse keep checking on patients who are sitting in the waiting area?

options.A: Doctors refuse to start treatment without fresh paperwork
options.B: A stable patient's condition can worsen while they wait
options.C: Patients get angry if their vital signs are not checked twice an hour
options.D: Hospital management requires nurses to update charts every five minutes

explanation: Illness can change fast! Someone who looked fine a few minutes ago can suddenly take a turn for the worse. Regular checks keep everyone safe. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which triage category is meant for a patient who needs life-saving help right this second?
explanation: Resuscitation is our highest alert level. Every single second counts here to keep the patient alive and stable! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h3)

question: A patient walks into the clinic with a mild ankle sprain and stable vital signs. What triage level fits best?
explanation: A stable injury that just needs a quick check or an X-ray falls right into our non-urgent category. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h3)

question: How is disaster triage different from regular emergency department triage?

options.A: Routine triage is only used when there are zero available beds
options.B: Disaster triage focuses on saving the greatest number with limited resources
options.C: Routine triage ignores vital signs while disaster triage requires full lab work
options.D: Disaster triage gives highest priority to patients with the worst chance of survival

explanation: When mass casualties hit, our main goal shifts from giving maximum individual care to saving the maximum number of community lives. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h4)

question: During a building collapse with dozens of victims, a patient with severe, fatal injuries gets an expectant (black) tag. Why do we do this?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to touch trauma patients outdoors
options.B: To preserve scarce medical supplies for victims who have a better chance of survival
options.C: Because minor injuries always take legal precedence over head trauma
options.D: To punish the patient for not wearing safety equipment

explanation: This is one of the hardest parts of nursing, but when supplies are limited, we must focus our efforts where we can genuinely save lives. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is a common misunderstanding about the role of the triage nurse?

options.A: That triage nurses are responsible for performing major surgical procedures
options.B: That the triage nurse works exclusively in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: That it is merely a clerical desk job rather than a high-level clinical assessment
options.D: That triage staff never interact directly with incoming patients

explanation: Triage is real clinical nursing! It takes sharp assessment skills and quick thinking to spot hidden dangers at the front desk. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is the triage nurse's job considered to carry big legal responsibilities?

options.A: A missed critical symptom during the initial sort can cause severe patient harm
options.B: Hospital insurance does not cover mistakes made outside the ward
options.C: Triage nurses must personally pay for any medication ordered at the desk
options.D: The nurse is legally required to diagnose every disease on arrival

explanation: Because triage is the very first stop, catching critical symptoms early protects the patient and keeps your clinical practice safe. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h5)

question: What quick assessment guide helps nurses check a new patient rapidly?

options.D: Primary survey (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure)

explanation: ABCDE is your best friend in emergency nursing. It lets you spot and tackle life-threatening issues instantly! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h6)

question: How is a triage check different from a full ward admission assessment?

options.A: Triage assessment is rapid and focused on immediate life threats rather than being comprehensive
options.B: Admission assessments take less than two minutes to complete
options.C: Admission assessments are always performed by security guards instead of nurses
options.D: Triage assessment skips vital signs entirely and relies on guesswork

explanation: At triage, we don't have time for a lengthy life story. We scan for immediate dangers first, then dive deeper later! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which ethical principle guides triage nurses to treat every patient fairly, no matter their background?
explanation: Justice means treating everyone fairly and sharing our healthcare resources impartially, without any bias or favoritism. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is good record-keeping at the triage desk so important for legal safety?

options.A: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment costs
options.B: It provides a clear record of when the patient arrived and their initial condition
options.C: It guarantees the hospital will win any lawsuit brought by insurance companies
options.D: It allows nurses to avoid writing shift reports at the end of the day

explanation: Clear notes prove exactly when the patient came in and how you cared for them. Good documentation is your best legal shield! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h7)
